basics.name: Man Yeung (Andy) Tai
basics.label: Postdoctoral Researcher, Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine (IKIM), University Hospital Essen
basics.summary: My research develops federated and privacy-preserving machine learning for trustworthy AI in medicine: methods that let clinical models learn from distributed hospital data without centralizing patient records, with explicit accounting of communication cost, privacy, and reliability. It builds on a PhD in neuroscience in which I applied machine learning to addiction psychiatry, including overdose risk prediction and clinical decision support.

work.name: Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Medicine (IKIM), University Hospital Essen
work.summary: Jointly supervised by Prof. Jens Kleesiek (IKIM) and Prof. Michael Kamp (Kamp Lab, Lamarr Institute, TU Dortmund). Federated learning for medical data in the FLIP-IT project (NEXT.IN.NRW-funded), with Dr. Moon Kim.
highlights: FLIP-IT: federated chronic kidney disease risk prediction (P(CKD stage >= 3)) across general practice clinics using the Flower framework

Privacy design: patient-level DP-SGD with SecAgg+ secure aggregation, FedAvg, an RDP privacy accountant with one global (ε, δ) target and per-practice noise calibration, per-round monitoring of global and worst-practice AUROC and sensitivity

Developing privacy-preserving federated continual learning methods and an open-source benchmark toolkit; work in progress on activation and rank-code communication protocols

projects.name: FLIP-IT, Federated learning for medical data
projects.summary: IKIM, University Hospital Essen; NEXT.IN.NRW-funded. Federated Learning in Practice Networks, co-funded by the European Union and North Rhine-Westphalia, builds infrastructure for decentralized training of medical AI across general practices in NRW (consortium: IKIM, docport, Flower Labs, KVWL, KVNO; project lead: Dr. Nicolas Conze). I build federated chronic kidney disease risk prediction (P(CKD stage >= 3)) on the Flower framework, with a privacy design of patient-level DP-SGD and SecAgg+ secure aggregation, FedAvg, an RDP privacy accountant with one global (ε, δ) target and per-practice noise calibration, per-round monitoring of global and worst-practice AUROC and sensitivity, and a governance gate with membership-inference leakage audit and clinical and legal review before on-site deployment. With Prof. Jens Kleesiek, Prof. Michael Kamp, and Dr. Moon Kim. Project site: https://www.flipit-research.network/

projects.name: Brain-inspired federated continual learning for healthcare AI
projects.summary: Privacy-preserving federated continual learning algorithms (federated synaptic consolidation, federated hippocampal replay, predictive-coding federated learning) that let clinical models learn continuously from distributed hospital data without catastrophic forgetting; open-source benchmark toolkit.

projects.name: Activation and rank-code communication protocols for federated learning
projects.summary: Federated protocols in which clients communicate activation or rank codes (which units fire, and in what order) instead of model parameters, with pre-registered control arms and explicit communication-bitrate accounting.

projects.name: RAMP, Risk Assessment and Management Platform

projects.name: HAVA, Maritime criminal detection system
projects.summary: With Clause Technology and NCIS. Agentic system for detecting illegal fishing and maritime criminal behaviour: automated web scraping, NLP incident classification, BERT/NER entity resolution of vessels, locations, and organizations, LLM-assisted de-duplication, and a Dockerized MongoDB/PostgreSQL deployment.
